biography.plain_text: Richard C. Rowe Sr, known as Dick, was an American marine-engine manufacturer and co-founder of Indmar. After twenty years in the US Marine Corps, he and his wife Donna started a small marine and industrial distributorship in 1971. They built it into a family-owned inboard-engine business that became a major supplier to recreational boat manufacturers.
biography.html: Richard C. Rowe Sr, known as Dick, was an American marine-engine manufacturer and co-founder of Indmar. After twenty years in the US Marine Corps, he and his wife Donna started a small marine and industrial distributorship in 1971. They built it into a family-owned inboard-engine business that became a major supplier to recreational boat manufacturers.

confidence.reason: Indmar's official memorial directly supports the identity, twenty-year Marine Corps service, co-founding with Donna, year and initial business model; the court record and specialist press support family ownership, manufacturing and commercial growth.

long_biography.plain_text:
Indmar grew out of Richard C. Rowe Sr's willingness to adapt industrial machinery for boats. Its first products included pumps built around automotive V8 engines. When jetboat builders requested marinised inboards, Rowe moved beyond assembling off-the-shelf parts and began making major components to his own durability standards.

That practical work developed into wider industry leadership. Rowe represented small marine-engine manufacturers during federal emissions consultations, donated engines for regulatory testing and advocated workable pollution controls. The National Marine Manufacturers Association recognised those contributions with its Chapman Award and Hall of Fame induction.
